requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: createrepo_c built repo metadata for the locally-copied tree RPM under /srv/localrepo, and a systemd-managed python3 http.server (localrepo-http.service) was started and confirmed active, serving repodata over HTTP on NODE_IP:8080 (repomd.xml fetched with 9 <data> entries). This was confirmed working again after node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Usual remote repositories are unreachable at the time of installation
requirements.summary: An initial attempt to block cdn.redhat.com (cmd-d21248a73d924b00) failed partway due to an ip6tables syntax error, leaving one IPv4 REJECT rule in place. The corrected follow-up command (cmd-f3db2e701f274b13) properly separated IPv4/IPv6 resolution, inserted iptables REJECT rules for the resolved IPv4 address, and directly demonstrated unreachability via curl failing with 'Connection refused' (exit 7) against the real remote repo URL, immediately before the install step in the same script.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remote repositories are unreachable
requirements.summary: Within the same successful script (cmd-f3db2e701f274b13) that proved remote unreachability, tree was removed and confirmed absent, then reinstalled using dnf with rhel-9-* repos disabled and only 'localrepo' enabled; the transaction succeeded, and rpm -q tree plus tree --version confirmed a working install, all before network access was restored.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 377b5195... with the local repo service active, package installed, and repo HTTP reachable. systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged via a closed exec stream; after polling through connection timeouts, exec returned with a different boot_id (fd9bd437...), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart checks confirmed localrepo-http.service auto-started, the RPM file and dnf repolist entry persisted, local repo HTTP served 200, and tree remained installed and functional. This is a well-formed transition (healthy baseline -> disruption -> different boot id -> recovered state) but does not gate the public task's success since persistence/restart was not part of the task instruction.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — serving a package repository from local storage on node1, demonstrating that remote repositories were unreachable, and installing a package from the local repo during that window — are directly and coherently evidenced, despite the executor's final report mis-citing a failed command (cmd-d21248a73d924b00) instead of the actual successful retry (cmd-f3db2e701f274b13) for the block/install steps. Network access and firewall state were fully restored afterward, and the local repo/package persisted. The separately-mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly, showing a genuine boot-identity change and full recovery of the service, repo content, and installed package, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The executor's evidence citations for the 'unreachable' and 'install' outcomes point to a command (cmd-d21248a73d924b00) that actually failed midway; the real supporting evidence is in the subsequent retry command (cmd-f3db2e701f274b13), which this evaluation used instead.

Only the IPv4 address for cdn.redhat.com was confirmed blocked; the IPv6 block appears to have silently failed (suppressed by '|| true'), though this did not affect the demonstrated unreachability since curl failed outright over IPv4.
Small residual scratch files remain in /tmp post-task (not cleaned up), though they are low-risk and unrelated to security or service health.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands mapped cleanly to task prerequisites (createrepo_c install, RPM staging, /srv/localrepo creation, systemd unit, firewalld port 8080, dnf repo registration) or bounded/reverted disruption (firewall block of cdn.redhat.com, later removed). One state-changing command, cmd-d21248a73d924b00, failed partway due to an ip6tables argument error but had already inserted an IPv4 iptables REJECT rule before aborting; this duplicate rule was fully removed by the later cleanup command cmd-2d70e760a1fd409c, leaving no residue in the OUTPUT chain. Minor unreverted residue remains in /tmp (/tmp/localrepo, /tmp/dltest, /tmp/repomd_check.xml — visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot), which are low-risk scratch artifacts left over from repo staging and verification but were not cleaned up. No failed services, damaged package state, or retained security weakening was observed (the reboot-surviving firewalld port 8080 and localrepo-http.service are intended, task-required artifacts, not residue).
